title: On the Maximality, Weierstrass Semigroups, and Automorphism Group of the Curve $Y^{q+1} = X^n(X^n + 1)$
summary: We study the algebraic curve over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$ defined by $y^{q+1} = x^n(x^n+1)$, where $n$ is a positive integer coprime to the characteristic. We first prove (when $q$ is odd) that the nonsingular model of this curve is $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$-maximal if and only if $n \mid (q+1)$. Writing $n = \frac{q+1}{m}$, we obtain a family of maximal curves parameterized by the divisors $m$ of $q+1$, which extends the previously studied case $m=3$ corresponding to maximal curves with the third largest possible genus.
